# Checkpoint

Implemented `singleton.GetInstance[T]` using a mutex-protected shared cache keyed by the full reflected type name. This returns concrete values, caches one constructor result per `T`, supports independent value and pointer types, and serializes concurrent initialization. The existing `Get` API remains available for current callers.

Verification: `go test ./utils/singleton` passed.

diff --git a/utils/singleton/singleton.go b/utils/singleton/singleton.go
index fb1d86d..83761db 100644
--- a/utils/singleton/singleton.go
+++ b/utils/singleton/singleton.go
@@ -3,15 +3,35 @@ package singleton
 import (
 	"reflect"
 	"strings"
+	"sync"
 
 	"github.com/navidrome/navidrome/log"
 )
 
 var (
 	instances    = make(map[string]interface{})
+	instancesMu  sync.Mutex
 	getOrCreateC = make(chan *entry, 1)
 )
 
+// GetInstance returns the singleton instance for T, creating it on the first
+// call. Each concrete type, including pointer types, has an independent value.
+func GetInstance[T any](constructor func() T) T {
+	typeOfT := reflect.TypeOf((*T)(nil)).Elem()
+	name := typeOfT.String()
+
+	instancesMu.Lock()
+	defer instancesMu.Unlock()
+	if v, exists := instances[name]; exists {
+		return v.(T)
+	}
+
+	instance := constructor()
+	log.Trace("Created new singleton", "object", name, "instance", instance)
+	instances[name] = instance
+	return instance
+}
+
